ALPHABET CENTER · LETTER X

Letter X — Xylophone.

The letters X x arrive with a red xylophone. X is the alphabet’s shape-shifter: it rarely starts words, and when it does — as in xylophone — it secretly sounds like z.

Meet the letter, hear its sound, trace it together — then play. Everything on this page is free, gentle and paced for you.

THE LETTER SOUND

What does X say?

“x — usually the ks at the end of fox and box”

X is a shape-shifter. In xylophone, the x actually starts with a z sound. Most of the time x says ks at the END of words: fox, box, six. Say fox slowly and hear the x hiding at the finish.

X’s sound usually hides at the end of words — fox, box, six. Practice it there, where it really lives.

TRACE THE LETTER

Trace X x together.

Follow the numbers with a finger — on screen or on each other’s palms. The arrows show the way to go, the numbers show where to start, and a grown-up reads the little script below each card. Slow and wobbly is exactly right.

Trace the uppercase X

Start at 1 at the top left, slide down to the bottom right. Lift. Start at 2 at the top right, slide down to the bottom left. The two lines cross in the middle.

Trace the lowercase x

Start at 1 at the top left, slide down to the bottom right. Lift. Start at 2 at the top right, slide down to the bottom left.

TAKE IT OFF SCREEN

X marks the spot.

Two minutes is plenty. Follow your child’s lead and stop while it is still fun — that is the whole method.

  1. 01

    Draw a treasure map of a room and mark the treasure with a big X.

  2. 02

    Hunt for things whose names end with the ks sound: box, blocks, socks.

  3. 03

    Tap the final sound together: fo-ks, bo-ks, si-ks — then open the treasure (a snack counts).

PLAY & PRACTICE

Games that use this letter.

The games mix every letter — play them after meeting two or three letters, or any day your child asks. No scores, no timers, no wrong answers that count.
